news.title: 'Not sorry at all' - Spain's Dani Olmo claims Argentina coach ‘not telling truth’ about punch after World Cup final
news.lede: DANI OLMO has snubbed Roberto Ayala’s apology after being struck by the Argentina coach at the World Cup. Ayala thrusting a hand towards Olmo’s throat was just one part of the melee that followed the final in New Jersey. The right-handed jab appeared to come from absolutely nowhere as players and staff from both sides clashed after Spain‘s 1-0 win in extra-time. Ayala, 53, claimed it was in response to Olmo mouthing off.

news.title: Over 23 Million Football Fans Sign Petition Calling For Argentina To Be Banned From World Cup
news.lede: Fans were left furious after the World Cup final. By Syazwan Bahri | 27 Jul 2026, 04:08 PM. The viral petition, titled Argentina Out, attracted 23.3 million signatures from supporters across roughly 170 countries within a single week. The petition closed after Spain secured a 1-0 extra-time victory over Argentina in the final on 19 July.

news.title: World Cup 2026: Gianni Infantino tells Fifa critics to 'meditate, pray or watch football'
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016. Fifa president Gianni Infantino has told critics to "meditate, pray or watch a football match" instead of "spreading hate and false rumours" about his leadership, the governing body and the World Cup. In a 15-slide post on his personal Instagram account - reposted to Fifa's eight million followers - Infantino addressed "those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens" to affirm his belief that, while they were "busy planting seeds of hate", Fifa was delivering the "greatest event on earth". He said the World Cup "celebrated humanity at its best", adding that the 2026 tournament had "100% safety and security, only joy and happiness".

news.title: Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics for 'spreading hate' during World Cup in scathing social media rant
news.lede: The message was shared across 15 slides on his personal Instagram account, and also cross-posted on FIFA's platform, which is followed by more than eight million people. In his bizarre statement, Infantino defended the handling of the World Cup, which took place across the United States, Canada and Mexico, and claimed critics had 'missed all that joy and togetherness' of the tournament. He also accused people of 'spreading hate and false rumours' after the final that was won by Spain, and urged them to 'reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match' instead. "To all of you who missed watching kids, babies, grandparents, and parents come together for the beautiful game, I say sorry that the matches are now over and sorry that you missed all that joy and togetherness," Infantino wrote.

news.title: Meet French football icon Zinedine Zidane’s son Luca, who played for Algeria at the World Cup
news.lede: French football legend Zinedine Zidane has fans going crazy after news broke that he has agreed to join the France national team as head coach. Sports newspaper L’Équipe reported that the 1998 Fifa World Cup winner will officially take the reins on September 1, with others reporting that his contract with Les Bleus runs till mid-2030. While Zizou is about to become France’s new coach, his son Luca Zidane, in contrast, stepped away from French football last September to join Algeria. He represented the North African nation at this World Cup, serving as the team’s starting goalkeeper despite a recent chin and jaw injury.

news.title: Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl
news.lede: Spain star Dani Olmo has refused to accept an apology from Argentina coach Roberto Ayala and accused him of lying about what happened following the World Cup final. There were violent clashes on the pitch after the full-time whistle crowned Spain as champions in New Jersey. Ferran Torres' goal in extra-time was enough to seal a 1-0 win for Spain, but their winning moment was tarnished by what followed.
